name: VA-09
label: Safe R

key_factors: District lean of R+22 in a heavily Republican Appalachian seat
Incumbent Morgan Griffith running with a large cash advantage ($974k on hand vs $14k)
Prediction markets price Democratic chances at about 2%
No polls or expert ratings available
model.rationale: The fundamentals point overwhelmingly to Griffith: a deep-red district, incumbency, and a lopsided fundraising edge, with markets pricing a Democratic win at roughly 2%. No polling or ratings justify moving away from the baseline.
model.watch: A major late-breaking scandal or a dramatic national wave toward Democrats could narrow the margin, though a flip remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Morgan Griffith seeks another term in a southwestern Virginia district that leans heavily Republican, with a partisan baseline of about 22 points in the GOP's favor. He enters the general election with a large financial advantage, holding roughly $974,000 on hand after raising nearly $1.8 million, while Democrat Joy Powers has raised about $85,000 and has just under $14,000 available. No outside groups have invested meaningfully in the race.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the contest, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and money, all of which favor the incumbent. Prediction markets give Democrats only a small chance of an upset. The race is rated Safe R, with the main uncertainty being the size of Griffith's winning margin rather than the outcome itself.
